Yes, size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement is currently considered an available treatment option in modern aortic surgery for patients with poststenotic dilatation of the aorta without impairment of the sinotubular junction of the aortic valve and root. This procedure involves the use of external reinforcement to reduce the size of the aorta, thereby improving its functionality and reducing symptoms associated with the condition.

This approach is often preferred over other methods that may not provide the same level of improvement in patients who are seeking surgical intervention due to poststenotic dilatation. The safety and efficacy of this procedure have been demonstrated in various studies, and it can be an option for eligible patients, although it's essential to note that each case should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

It is crucial for patients considering size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement to discuss their individual situation, medical history, and the potential benefits and risks associated with this procedure with a qualified healthcare professional.
